doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27

title: Tony Sbarbaro's visit to New Orleans
summary: Wiggs asks if Laine saw drummer Tony Sbarbaro, who made a short carnival trip; his mother was Gabe Pounders's sister.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Let's see. When I have, when I did, if I got that picture.
Did you see, what's the, anything of his name, the drummer with the Dixie Man jazz band when he was in town.
Tony Sparbaro. Tony Sparbaro. Tony Spargo he calls himself now. Tony Sabarbara.
Tony Sabarbara. Did you see him when he was down for Carnival?
No, I wouldn't have ever. He was down for Carnival. Yeah. He was? Yeah. He was? Yeah. He was? Yeah. He was the one, he didn't come down to Chimmy.
He was only here, one, he had to leave the next day.

His mother, I believe, was sick or somebody in the family was sick, so he didn't get to see many people. He left right away. Very short trip. I saw him one day, just for a minute. Gabe, Gabe Pounders' sister is his mother. Who? Gabe Pounders, Tony Sabarbara. Tony Sabarbara. Yeah, I didn't know that. No. Yeah.
Yeah. Oh, in Chicago, New York.
